verdict: Roblox grew revenue 16% to $1.6B as 138 million daily users played nearly 34 billion hours, but it still lost $230M — and bookings, the cash players actually spent, fell 12% against last year's extraordinary surge.

segments.name: Platform revenue
segments.note: Sales of Robux (the platform's virtual currency) and subscriptions, recognized gradually over the ~27 months players are expected to keep spending. The cash collected upfront ('bookings') was $1,697M.

opex.name: Developer exchange fees
opex.note: The cut paid out to creators when players spend Robux in their games — Roblox raised creator pay rates this year.

opex.name: Infrastructure and trust & safety
opex.note: Servers and computing (including AI) plus the safety operation that polices the platform.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform, tools and AI features.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — includes $49M of legal settlement expenses this quarter.

takeaways.title: The audience is enormous
takeaways.text: Daily active users hit 138M and hours engaged reached nearly 34 billion in a single quarter — the platform's pull is not the problem.

takeaways.title: Bookings slipped
takeaways.text: Bookings — Robux cash sales — fell 12% YoY after 2025's viral surge, even as reported revenue rose 16%: revenue is recognized over ~27 months, so past bookings are still flowing through.

takeaways.title: Losses, but cash-positive
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was +$364M despite the $230M accounting loss: players pay upfront, and $298M of the quarter's costs were stock pay, not cash.

oneTimers: G&A includes $49M of legal settlement expenses tied to state youth-safety and consumer-protection matters — management treats them as outside the ordinary course of business.

Revenue is not the cash in: bookings were $1,697M but revenue was $1,572M. Roblox defers most bookings and recognizes them over the 27-month average paying-user lifetime, so reported revenue lags the cash by design.
otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$54M: $60M of interest earned on Roblox's investment pile, minus $11M of interest expense, plus $5M of other income.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference. Costs ran to $114.63 per $100 of revenue — the extra is the loss, covered by cash the company already had.
